transcript: I've spent a fair amount of time trying to understand the science around this and It is very clear that these foods that are genetically engineered are safe. And that's the first step. You can't get past that if they don't cross that hurdle. Not much else means anything. In fact, we had a hearing now a few months back where we had six witnesses, many of whom opposed what I'm trying to do legislatively, from the left and right, from food safety groups and from all across the world. But I asked every one of them directly, are genetically engineered foods equally safe to non-genetically engineered foods. And six for six, every witness testified that they were equally safe. And so I am very confident that our food safety processes are sufficient to make sure that the food that's being put in the American stores and American consumers are purchasing is a safer consumption. And with respect to labeling, I always want to make sure that people have the right to know what's in their food. I think that's certainly very, very important But I want to make sure that we have the capacity to continue to feed the world and have affordable food and a patchwork of state laws. Not just states, frankly, there are cities that would love to put labeling laws on genetically engineered foods will lead to enormous cost increases for consumers. And that's unacceptable to me for a product that is safe. So we're working to try and meet all the objectives of making sure consumers can, if they choose, purchase on GM foods, organic foods, whatever it is they prefer for their family. We'll make sure we still have the technology to feed the world.
